# MM-P3-L4-HT02-S2 - Fastener inspection and torque - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2
Revision: Rev F (this revision supersedes Rev E)  
Plant: P3, line P3-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-HT02

Scope
This document establishes the required fastener inspection and torque verification practices for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02). It covers inspection rationale, permitted tools, step-by-step procedure for visual and functional checks during preventive maintenance and reactive servicing, and clear acceptance criteria. This procedure supports safe mechanical integrity and repeatable process conditions that affect quench timing and furnace seals. See related documents MM-P3-L4-HT02, SB-1043, SOP-P3-L4-01 for broader maintenance schedules, safety bulletins, and furnace operating procedures.

Background and rationale
Fasteners on EQ-P3-L4-HT02 secure components that influence alignment of quench delivery, furnace door seals, shielding, and mounting of sensors. Loose or improperly lubricated fasteners can permit movement that alters quench timing and introduces variability into heat treat cycles. Fastener threads that bind or gall can lead to under-torqued joints even when torque tools indicate target settings. Visual inspection combined with torque verification and proper lubrication reduces unplanned downtime, improves repeatability, and protects threaded components from wear.

Tools
- Calibrated torque wrench (see calibration records per SOP-P3-L4-01).  
- Clean, lint-free rags and inspection mirror.  
- Thread lubricant: The lubricant part number for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) is CFW-LUB-371.  
- Thread cleaning tools (non-abrasive brushes, compressed air per SB-1043).  
- Fastener identification tags and maintenance log forms.  
- Personal protective equipment per SOP-P3-L4-01.

Procedure
Preparation
- Review furnace history in MM-P3-L4-HT02 and confirm required maintenance window with operations. Lockout and de-energize as required by SOP-P3-L4-01 before accessing structural fasteners, door hardware, sensor mounts, and quench manifold connections.
- Gather required tools and lubricant CFW-LUB-371. Verify torque wrench calibration status per SOP-P3-L4-01.

Visual inspection
- Inspect all accessible external and internal fasteners for thread damage, corrosion, or evidence of movement (fretting, imprinting). Use an inspection mirror for hard-to-see locations.
- Check for missing fastener hardware or non-standard replacements. Tag any non-standard hardware and report per MM-P3-L4-HT02.
- Inspect mating faces and plug interfaces for burrs or debris that would prevent proper clamp-up. Clean with lint-free rags and approved cleaning procedures referenced in SB-1043.

Thread and bearing surface prep
- Where debris or old lubricant is present, clean threads and bearing surfaces using non-abrasive brushes and compressed air per SB-1043. Dry surfaces before applying lubricant.
- Apply a light, even film of CFW-LUB-371 to threads and bearing surfaces where specified by equipment manufacturer or MM-P3-L4-HT02. Avoid over-application; excess lubricant can affect torque-to-tension relationship.

Torque verification
- Seat fasteners by hand to ensure correct engagement of threads. Use torque wrench to apply torque smoothly to achieve uniform clamp-up. If resistance indicates thread damage or binding, back out and re-clean; replace fastener only after documenting condition and approval per MM-P3-L4-HT02.
- When re-torquing assemblies that include load-sharing components (e.g., flange assemblies, door hardware), follow manufacturer pattern to achieve uniform compression and alignment. Record each fastener's identification and the applied tool used.
- If a fastener cannot be brought to the expected feel of a snug, documented attempt, do not force; stop, tag, and escalate to maintenance engineering per MM-P3-L4-HT02.

Examples and special cases
- Example: If a door hinge fastener exhibits fretting and surface pitting such that thread engagement is compromised, tag the fastener and replace with a torque-rated equivalent. Document the condition and replacement in the maintenance record and reference SB-1043 for corrosion mitigation guidance.
- Example: Fastener in proximity to quench manifold showing residue build-up—clean, apply CFW-LUB-371, and verify seating per procedure. Note any residue source in the record to support follow-up on quench system integrity.

Records to keep
- For each maintenance action on EQ-P3-L4-HT02, complete the fastener inspection log and attach the torque verification sheet. Record equipment id EQ-P3-L4-HT02, maintenance date, technician name, fastener location, condition observed, lubricant applied (CFW-LUB-371), and any tags placed.
- Maintain calibration proof for torque wrench used, referenced to SOP-P3-L4-01 records. File nonconformance tags and corrective action reports per MM-P3-L4-HT02.

Acceptance criteria
- All inspected fasteners must be free of thread damage that compromises engagement. Surface corrosion or fretting that reduces safe engagement requires replacement and documentation.
- All fasteners requiring lubricant must have a uniform film of CFW-LUB-371 applied where specified. Evidence of lubricant omission is cause for rework.
- Fasteners must seat and allow the technician to achieve a secure, repeatable clamp-up using calibrated torque tools. Any fastener that cannot be secured without thread damage or binding must be tagged, removed, or replaced and recorded.
- Maintenance records for EQ-P3-L4-HT02 must include completed inspection log, torque verification sheet, lubricant usage entry for CFW-LUB-371, and references to related document actions in MM-P3-L4-HT02, SB-1043, and SOP-P3-L4-01.

Notes on quench timing relevance
The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) is 20 seconds. Fastener-related misalignment or leakage in quench manifolds can increase effective quench delay. Ensure fasteners on quench delivery assemblies are inspected and secured as part of this procedure to help maintain quench timing within acceptable process limits cited in MM-P3-L4-HT02.

Revision history
Rev F: Current content; supersedes Rev E. See MM-P3-L4-HT02 for prior revision trace and SB-1043 for corrosion handling guidance.
